correctness.rationale: For Q5 each fort has size at least 5, and every size-5 fort is exactly N(v), independently certified by exhaustive verification of every 1..5-subset (242824 cases). The construction has 4 disjoint 5-neighborhoods and an explicit disjoint size-8 fort. Any 6-fort packing must comprise 4 size-5 neighborhoods and 2 size-6 forts because 6*5=30 and 32 available vertices, while at most 4 neighborhoods can be pairwise disjoint. A counting lemma restricts each size-6 fort to parity profile (0,6),(1,5),(5,1),(6,0). Mixed cases contain a fifth disjoint neighborhood, impossible; each all-parity residual 6-set fails the fort condition at a vertex distance 2 from both same-parity neighborhood centers. Code checks all size-6 subsets and the construction and provides a re-runnable predicate. Scope only Q5; no inference from finite experimentation to higher d.

originality.rationale: The 2023 foundational paper arXiv:2310.17904v3 Proposition 3.15 establishes fractional zero forcing 2^d/d but leaves the integer fort number of the 5-cube unresolved. Full 2025 text arXiv:2507.10826v1 Theorem 3.8 classifies minimum forts and Corollary 3.12 gives only 4<=ft(Q5)<=6, with exact values in Theorem 3.13 for dimensions 2^k, excluding d=5. New exact value 5 and strict separation from open packing 4 are not consequences of these bounds and have not been identified in searched indexed records. Unindexed equivalent prior work remains a bounded residual risk.

value.rationale: Dimension five is the first case beyond the power-of-two family at which published fort-number bounds leave an integer gap. Resolving it determines a natural graph invariant, supplies a motivated exact finite cutoff, and demonstrates the genuinely larger packing capacity of non-minimum forts: ft(Q5)=5 but rho^o(Q5)=4. The obstruction argument classifies why the tempting six-fort tiling cannot occur; value is not claimed from code or exactness alone. No downstream general theorem is asserted.
